# Sebago (01, engineer) — BAD-034

## Brief
Make scripts/worktree-init.sh link admin/node_modules from the main checkout the same way it links the root node_modules, and add the admin link to the parallel-worktrees skill's sentence listing what the script wires.

Context: admin/ is its own npm package with its own dependency tree. A fresh worktree gets the root node_modules symlink and every voicepack but no admin/node_modules, so a worktree that touches admin/ cannot run its typecheck, lint or build, and the parallel-worktrees skill forbids npm install inside a worktree. BAD-031's worktree hit exactly this: the script reported node_modules linked and 23 voicepacks linked while `ls admin/node_modules` said No such file or directory.

Required behaviour, mirroring the existing root block (same -L test, same three outcomes, same messages with the admin/ path in them):
- admin/node_modules is a symlink: report it as present with its target.
- admin/node_modules is a real directory: report size and say RELINK=1 replaces it; with RELINK=1 and $MAIN/admin/node_modules present, replace it with the symlink and report the space reclaimed.
- absent and $MAIN/admin/node_modules exists: ln -s it and report the link.
- $MAIN/admin/node_modules missing: report it and how to fix (npm ci in admin/ of the main checkout). Decide whether that should exit 1 like the root block or only warn, and say why in your result; a worktree that never touches admin/ should still get wired, so a warning is the better default unless you find a reason otherwise.
Keep the script's comment style and its "Safe to re-run" promise. Put the block right after the root node_modules block, under the same dependencies heading, and keep `set -euo pipefail` honest (no unset variables, no pipeline that fails on an absent path).

Skill edit: in .claude/skills/parallel-worktrees/SKILL.md the sentence "It links `node_modules` and every voicepack, mints the gitignored ..." must also name `admin/node_modules`; touch nothing else in that file unless the RELINK paragraph (around line 44) needs the admin link mentioned to stay true.

Proof, run from this worktree, which is fresh (EnterWorktree created it minutes ago and nothing has wired it yet):
1. `bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` once: paste the dependency lines of its output and `ls -l admin/node_modules` showing a symlink to /Users/ericlugo/Personal/BadTakes/admin/node_modules.
2. Run it again: output shows both links as already present, nothing changes (`git status --short` stays empty; node_modules paths are gitignored).
3. Simulate the private-copy case: `rm admin/node_modules`, then `mkdir admin/node_modules`, run the script without RELINK and show the warning, then `RELINK=1 bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` and show the symlink is back.
4. `bash -n scripts/worktree-init.sh` and, if shellcheck is on PATH, `shellcheck scripts/worktree-init.sh` (report if it is absent; do not install it).
5. From the worktree, run admin's typecheck once (`npm --prefix admin run typecheck`, or whatever admin/package.json names) to show the linked tree actually serves a worktree; report the result, and if it fails for a reason unrelated to the link, say so with the error.
Do not run npm install anywhere. Do not create or remove git worktrees (the hook refuses git worktree for you; this worktree is the fresh one). The harness refuses compound shell (&&, ;, pipes into files) from this worktree session: run plain, single commands.
